results.content: {"action":"fetch","data":{"node":{"body":"To stop navigation keybindings (and 'q'=quit) from firing while a user types into a field, the runtime keeps `UiState.input_mode_active` (declared src/ui.rs lines 414-416) in sync and uses it as a global filter. `App::sync_input_mode` (src/app.rs lines 576-612) asks the currently-active screen whether any text input is focused (via each Screen's `is_input_focused()`), with a catch-all `_ => false`. It is called at the START of `handle_event` (line 652) and again after each handled event in `run` (line 312), so the flag reflects focus before global handlers run.\n\n`App::get_action` (lines 616-648) is the choke point: when `input_mode_active` is true it only lets through an allowlist of editing/navigation-safe actions (Cancel, Confirm, NextTab, PrevTab, Help, Backspace, DeleteChar, Home, End, MoveLeft, MoveRight, and MoveUp/MoveDown which individual screens disambiguate) and returns `None` for everything else, so plain letter keys reach the field as text. This is the mechanism behind CLAUDE.md Critical Rule #5 ('Guard text input focus ... or q will quit instead of typing'): the rule is enforced centrally here, but only works if a new screen reports its focus through `is_input_focused()` and gets an arm in `sync_input_mode`'s match — otherwise the guard silently no-ops for that screen.","kind":"task","type":"knowledge","title":"Text-input focus gates the keymap: input_mode_active is recomputed every event and filters navigation actions in get_action","status":"active","version":1,"category":"architecture","short_id":"KNOW-195","created_at":"2026-06-29T16:12:59+00:00","updated_at":"2026-06-29T16:12:59+00:00","source_type":"import","anchor_files":["src/app.rs","src/ui.rs"],"anchor_symbols":["App::sync_input_mode","App::get_action","UiState","input_mode_active"],"created_by":"attempt-9ea36371dc3a34ac2cc46ae21dda18f0@example.dev","staleness":"fresh","verification":"verified"},"edges":[{"dir":"in","rel":"relates-to","node":"KNOW-196","title":"In text-input popups, insert plain Char keys BEFORE keymap lookup or vim bindings (h/l/j/k/q) get eaten as navigation"}],"id":"KNOW-195","title":"Text-input focus gates the keymap: input_mode_active is recomputed every event and filters navigation actions in get_action","url":"https://app.stele-ai.dev/p/dotstate-dotfile-manager-47d7a436b18b/nodes/KNOW-195"}}

{"action":"fetch","data":{"node":{"body":"Recurring hard-won pattern duplicated across nearly every screen with a text field: when a text-input popup/field is open, a plain `KeyCode::Char(c)` with no CONTROL/ALT/SUPER modifier must be inserted into the TextInput FIRST and the handler must return early, BEFORE the code looks up the keymap action. Reason: under the Vim keymap preset, characters like h/l/j/k/q are bound to MoveLeft/Right/Down/Up/Quit; if the keymap is consulted first, typing the letter 'q' into a profile name or token would quit the app and 'h' would move the cursor instead of inserting the character. The literal guard is `if let KeyCode::Char(c) = key.code { if !key.modifiers.intersects(KeyModifiers::CONTROL | KeyModifiers::ALT | KeyModifiers::SUPER) { <field>.insert_char(c); return Ok(ScreenAction::Refresh); } }`. Locations carrying the comment 'ALWAYS insert the character first / This ensures vim bindings like h/l don't interfere with typing': storage_setup.rs:943, dotfile_selection.rs:2313, manage_profiles.rs:1329/1637/1712, profile_selection.rs:427, manage_packages.rs:1158. {"action":"fetch","data":{"node":{"body":"The CLAUDE.md rule 'Guard text input focus' is enforced through two cooperating layers, not just inside each screen. Layer 1: each controller's `is_input_focused()` reports whether a TextInput is actively being typed into (e.g. StorageSetupScreen returns true only when focus==Form AND the focused field is a text field AND, in reconfiguration, only token+editing — storage_setup.rs:1400; ManagePackagesScreen returns true for Add/Edit/Delete/Import popups — manage_packages.rs:636; MainMenuScreen and SyncWithRemoteScreen hardcode false since they have no inputs). Layer 2: App::sync_input_mode() (src/app.rs:576-612) calls the active screen's is_input_focused() and stores it in `ui_state.input_mode_active`; then App::get_action() (src/app.rs:616) consults that flag and, when in input mode, SUPPRESSES navigation actions but still always lets through Action::Cancel | Confirm | NextTab | PrevTab | Help (app.rs:624-630). Consequence: a screen that forgets to report input focus will have 'q'/'h'/'j'/'k' interpreted as nav/quit while the user is typing. 40	    /// Get the action for a key event, checking overrides first then preset
41	    /// Note: If an action is overridden, preset bindings for that action are ignored
42	    #[must_use]
43	    pub fn get_action(&self, code: KeyCode, modifiers: KeyModifiers) -> Option<Action> {
44	        // Use all_bindings which already handles override shadowing
45	        for binding in self.all_bindings() {
46	            if binding.matches(code, modifiers) {
47	                return Some(binding.action);
48	            }
49	        }
50	        None
51	    }

53	    /// Get all bindings (overrides + preset) for display in help
54	    /// Overrides shadow preset bindings for the same action
55	    #[must_use]
56	    pub fn all_bindings(&self) -> Vec<KeyBinding> {
57	        let mut bindings = self.overrides.clone();
58	        let preset_bindings = self.preset.bindings();
59	
60	        // Add preset bindings that aren't overridden
61	        for preset_binding in preset_bindings {
62	            let is_overridden = self
63	                .overrides
64	                .iter()
65	                .any(|o| o.action == preset_binding.action);
66	            if !is_overridden {
67	                bindings.push(preset_binding);
68	            }
69	        }
70	
71	        bindings
72	    }

79	        let down_key = self.get_key_display_for_action(Action::MoveDown);
80	        format!("{up_key}/{down_key}")

87	        let quit_key = self.get_key_display_for_action(Action::Quit);
88	        let cancel_key = self.get_key_display_for_action(Action::Cancel);
89	        if quit_key == cancel_key {
90	            quit_key
91	        } else {

103	    /// Get the display string for a specific action (e.g., `Action::Quit` -> "q")
104	    /// Checks overrides first, then preset. Returns generic fallback if not found.
105	    #[must_use]
106	    pub fn get_key_display_for_action(&self, action: Action) -> String {
107	        // Check overrides
108	        if let Some(binding) = self.overrides.iter().find(|b| b.action == action) {
109	            return binding.display();
110	        }
111	
112	        // Check preset
113	        if let Some(binding) = self
114	            .preset
115	            .bindings()
116	            .into_iter()
117	            .find(|b| b.action == action)
118	        {
119	            return binding.display();
120	        }
121	
122	        // Fallback for actions not in current map (shouldn't happen for core actions)
123	        format!("{action:?}")
124	    }

19	/// A widget for rendering `TextInput` with consistent styling.
20	///
21	/// # Example
22	/// ```
23	/// use dotstate::widgets::TextInputWidget;
24	/// use dotstate::utils::TextInput;
25	/// use ratatui::widgets::Block;
26	///
27	/// let input = TextInput::with_text("hello");
28	/// let widget = TextInputWidget::new(&input)

30	///     .placeholder("Enter username...")
31	///     .focused(true);
32	/// // frame.render_widget(widget, area);
33	/// ```
34	pub struct TextInputWidget<'a> {
35	    /// Reference to the text input state
36	    input: &'a TextInput,
37	    /// Title for the input field
38	    title: Option<&'a str>,
39	    /// Placeholder text when empty
40	    placeholder: Option<&'a str>,
41	    /// Whether the input is focused
42	    focused: bool,
43	    /// Whether the input is disabled
44	    disabled: bool,
45	    /// Title alignment
46	    title_alignment: Alignment,

50	    block: Option<Block<'a>>,

53	impl<'a> TextInputWidget<'a> {
54	    /// Create a new text input widget.
55	    #[must_use]
56	    pub fn new(input: &'a TextInput) -> Self {
57	        Self {
58	            input,
59	            title: None,

61	            focused: false,
62	            disabled: false,

99	    pub fn title_alignment(mut self, alignment: Alignment) -> Self {
100	        self.title_alignment = alignment;

114	        self.block = Some(block);

116	    }

118	    /// Get the display text (actual text, masked text, or placeholder).
119	    fn display_text(&self) -> String {
120	        let text = self.input.text();
121	
122	        if text.is_empty() {
123	            self.placeholder.unwrap_or("").to_string()
124	        } else if self.masked {
125	            // Mask with bullets (same length as actual text)
126	            "•".repeat(text.chars().count())
127	        } else {
128	            text.to_string()
129	        }
130	    }
131	
132	    /// Get the text style based on state.
133	    fn text_style(&self) -> Style {
134	        if self.disabled {
135	            disabled_text_style()
136	        } else if self.input.is_empty() {
137	            input_placeholder_style()
138	        } else {
139	            input_text_style()
140	        }
141	    }
142	
143	    /// Get the border style based on state.
144	    fn border_style(&self) -> Style {
145	        if self.disabled {
146	            disabled_border_style()
147	        } else if self.focused {
148	            focused_border_style()
149	        } else {
150	            unfocused_border_style()
151	        }
152	    }
153	
154	    /// Create the block for the input.
155	    fn create_block(&self) -> Block<'a> {
156	        if let Some(block) = &self.block {
157	            // Use custom block but override border style
158	            block.clone().border_style(self.border_style())
159	        } else {
160	            // Default block
161	            let mut block = Block::default()
162	                .borders(Borders::ALL)
163	                .border_type(crate::styles::theme().border_type(self.focused))
164	                .border_style(self.border_style())
165	                .style(crate::styles::theme().background_style());
166	
167	            if let Some(title) = self.title {
168	                block = block
169	                    .title(format!(" {title} "))
170	                    .title_alignment(self.title_alignment);
171	            }
172	
173	            block
174	        }
175	    }
176	}

178	impl Widget for TextInputWidget<'_> {
179	    fn render(self, area: Rect, buf: &mut Buffer) {
180	        let block = self.create_block();
181	        let inner = block.inner(area);
182	
183	        // Render the paragraph
184	        let paragraph = Paragraph::new(self.display_text())
185	            .block(block)
186	            .style(self.text_style());
187	
188	        paragraph.render(area, buf);
189	
190	        // Set cursor position if focused and not disabled
191	        if self.focused && !self.disabled {
192	            let cursor_pos = self.input.cursor();
193	            let clamped_cursor = cursor_pos.min(self.input.text().chars().count());
194	            let x = inner.x + clamped_cursor.min(inner.width as usize) as u16;
195	            let y = inner.y;
196	
197	            // Set cursor in buffer metadata (Frame will handle actual positioning)
198	            if let Some(cell) = buf.cell_mut((x, y)) {
199	                cell.set_skip(false);
200	            }
201	        }
202	    }
203	}

208	/// to properly set the cursor position.

211	    fn render_text_input_widget(&mut self, widget: TextInputWidget, area: Rect);

215	    fn render_text_input_widget(&mut self, widget: TextInputWidget, area: Rect) {
216	        let focused = widget.focused;
217	        let disabled = widget.disabled;
218	        let cursor_pos = widget.input.cursor();
219	        let text = widget.input.text();
220	
221	        // Calculate block inner area for cursor positioning

223	        let inner = block.inner(area);
224	
225	        // Render the widget
226	        self.render_widget(widget, area);
227	
228	        // Set cursor position if focused and not disabled
229	        if focused && !disabled {
230	            let clamped_cursor = cursor_pos.min(text.chars().count());
231	            let x = inner.x + clamped_cursor.min(inner.width as usize) as u16;
232	            let y = inner.y;
233	            self.set_cursor_position((x, y));
234	        }

216	/// Handle text input for a single character insertion
217	///
218	/// # Arguments
219	/// * `text` - Mutable reference to the text string
220	/// * `cursor_pos` - Mutable reference to cursor position
221	/// * `c` - Character to insert
222	fn handle_char_insertion(text: &mut String, cursor_pos: &mut usize, c: char) {
223	    if c.is_ascii() && !c.is_control() {
224	        let byte_index = text
225	            .char_indices()
226	            .map(|(i, _)| i)
227	            .nth(*cursor_pos)
228	            .unwrap_or(text.len());
229	        text.insert(byte_index, c);
230	        *cursor_pos = (*cursor_pos + 1).min(text.chars().count());
231	    }
232	}

234	/// Handle cursor movement
235	///
236	/// # Arguments
237	/// * `text` - The text string
238	/// * `cursor_pos` - Mutable reference to cursor position
239	/// * `key_code` - Key code (Left, Right, Home, End)
240	fn handle_cursor_movement(text: &str, cursor_pos: &mut usize, key_code: KeyCode) {
241	    match key_code {
242	        KeyCode::Left if *cursor_pos > 0 => {
243	            *cursor_pos -= 1;
244	        }
245	        KeyCode::Right => {
246	            let char_count = text.chars().count();
247	            if *cursor_pos < char_count {
248	                *cursor_pos += 1;
249	            }
250	        }
251	        KeyCode::Home => {
252	            *cursor_pos = 0;
253	        }
254	        KeyCode::End => {
255	            *cursor_pos = text.chars().count();
256	        }
257	        _ => {}
258	    }
259	}

261	/// Handle character deletion (backspace)
262	///
263	/// # Arguments
264	/// * `text` - Mutable reference to the text string
265	/// * `cursor_pos` - Mutable reference to cursor position
266	fn handle_backspace(text: &mut String, cursor_pos: &mut usize) {
267	    if *cursor_pos > 0 {
268	        let before_cursor = text.chars().take(*cursor_pos - 1);
269	        let after_cursor = text.chars().skip(*cursor_pos);
270	        *text = before_cursor.chain(after_cursor).collect();
271	        *cursor_pos -= 1;
272	    }
273	}
274	
275	/// Handle character deletion (delete key)
276	///
277	/// # Arguments
278	/// * `text` - Mutable reference to the text string
279	/// * `cursor_pos` - Mutable reference to cursor position
280	fn handle_delete(text: &mut String, cursor_pos: &mut usize) {
281	    let char_count = text.chars().count();
282	    if *cursor_pos < char_count {
283	        let before_cursor = text.chars().take(*cursor_pos);
284	        let after_cursor = text.chars().skip(*cursor_pos + 1);
285	        *text = before_cursor.chain(after_cursor).collect();
286	    }
287	}
288	/// Handle generic input for text fields (movement, editing)
289	///
290	/// # Arguments
291	/// * `text` - Mutable reference to the text string
292	/// * `cursor_pos` - Mutable reference to cursor position
293	/// * `key_code` - Key code from event
294	fn handle_input(text: &mut String, cursor_pos: &mut usize, key_code: KeyCode) {
295	    match key_code {
296	        KeyCode::Char(c) => handle_char_insertion(text, cursor_pos, c),
297	        KeyCode::Backspace => handle_backspace(text, cursor_pos),
298	        KeyCode::Delete => handle_delete(text, cursor_pos),
299	        KeyCode::Left | KeyCode::Right | KeyCode::Home | KeyCode::End => {
300	            handle_cursor_movement(text, cursor_pos, key_code);
301	        }
302	        _ => {}
303	    }
304	}

34	pub struct TextInputWidget<'a> {

118	    /// Get the display text (actual text, masked text, or placeholder).
119	    fn display_text(&self) -> String {
120	        let text = self.input.text();
121	
122	        if text.is_empty() {

132	    /// Get the text style based on state.
133	    fn text_style(&self) -> Style {
134	        if self.disabled {

136	        } else if self.input.is_empty() {

138	        } else {

155	    fn create_block(&self) -> Block<'a> {
156	        if let Some(block) = &self.block {

178	impl Widget for TextInputWidget<'_> {
179	    fn render(self, area: Rect, buf: &mut Buffer) {
180	        let block = self.create_block();
181	        let inner = block.inner(area);
182	
183	        // Render the paragraph
184	        let paragraph = Paragraph::new(self.display_text())
185	            .block(block)
186	            .style(self.text_style());
187	
188	        paragraph.render(area, buf);
189	
190	        // Set cursor position if focused and not disabled
191	        if self.focused && !self.disabled {
192	            let cursor_pos = self.input.cursor();
193	            let clamped_cursor = cursor_pos.min(self.input.text().chars().count());
194	            let x = inner.x + clamped_cursor.min(inner.width as usize) as u16;
195	            let y = inner.y;
196	
197	            // Set cursor in buffer metadata (Frame will handle actual positioning)
198	            if let Some(cell) = buf.cell_mut((x, y)) {
199	                cell.set_skip(false);
200	            }
201	        }
202	    }
203	}

4	/// A text input field with encapsulated state.
5	///
6	/// This struct wraps the text and cursor position, providing a cleaner API
7	/// for managing text input in forms and screens.
8	///
9	/// # Example
10	/// ```
11	/// use dotstate::utils::text_input::TextInput;
12	///
13	/// let mut input = TextInput::new();
14	/// input.insert_char('h');
15	/// input.insert_char('i');
16	/// assert_eq!(input.text(), "hi");
17	/// ```
18	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
19	pub struct TextInput {
20	    text: String,
21	    cursor: usize,
22	}
23	
24	impl TextInput {
25	    /// Create a new empty text input.
26	    #[must_use]
27	    pub fn new() -> Self {
28	        Self::default()
29	    }
30	
31	    /// Create a text input with initial text.
32	    pub fn with_text(text: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
33	        let text = text.into();
34	        let cursor = text.chars().count();
35	        Self { text, cursor }
36	    }
37	
38	    /// Get the current text as a string slice.
39	    #[must_use]
40	    pub fn text(&self) -> &str {
41	        &self.text
42	    }
43	
44	    /// Get the current cursor position.
45	    #[must_use]
46	    pub fn cursor(&self) -> usize {
47	        self.cursor
48	    }
49	
50	    /// Get the trimmed text.
51	    #[must_use]
52	    pub fn text_trimmed(&self) -> &str {
53	        self.text.trim()
54	    }
55	
56	    /// Check if the text is empty (no characters at all). Matches
57	    /// `TextInputWidget::display_text` so the widget styles placeholder
58	    /// vs. typed text consistently — typing whitespace renders the
59	    /// whitespace rather than staying invisible as a "placeholder".
60	    /// For validation that should reject whitespace-only input, callers
61	    /// should use `text_trimmed().is_empty()`.
62	    #[must_use]
63	    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
64	        self.text.is_empty()
65	    }
66	
67	    /// Set the text and move cursor to end.
68	    pub fn set_text(&mut self, text: impl Into<String>) {
69	        self.text = text.into();
70	        self.cursor = self.text.chars().count();
71	    }
72	
73	    /// Clear the text and reset cursor.
74	    pub fn clear(&mut self) {
75	        self.text.clear();
76	        self.cursor = 0;
77	    }
78	
79	    /// Insert a character at the cursor position.
80	    pub fn insert_char(&mut self, c: char) {
81	        handle_char_insertion(&mut self.text, &mut self.cursor, c);
82	    }
83	
84	    /// Delete the character before the cursor (backspace).
85	    pub fn backspace(&mut self) {
86	        handle_backspace(&mut self.text, &mut self.cursor);
87	    }
88	
89	    /// Delete the character at the cursor position.
90	    pub fn delete(&mut self) {
91	        handle_delete(&mut self.text, &mut self.cursor);
92	    }
93	
94	    /// Move the cursor left.
95	    pub fn move_left(&mut self) {
96	        if self.cursor > 0 {
97	            self.cursor -= 1;
98	        }
99	    }
100	
101	    /// Move the cursor right.
102	    pub fn move_right(&mut self) {
103	        let char_count = self.text.chars().count();
104	        if self.cursor < char_count {
105	            self.cursor += 1;
106	        }
107	    }
108	
109	    /// Move the cursor to the start.
110	    pub fn move_home(&mut self) {
111	        self.cursor = 0;
112	    }
113	
114	    /// Move the cursor to the end.
115	    pub fn move_end(&mut self) {
116	        self.cursor = self.text.chars().count();
117	    }
118	
119	    /// Handle a key code event.
120	    ///
121	    /// Returns true if the key was handled.
122	    pub fn handle_key(&mut self, key_code: KeyCode) -> bool {
123	        handle_input(&mut self.text, &mut self.cursor, key_code);
124	        matches!(
125	            key_code,
126	            KeyCode::Char(_)
127	                | KeyCode::Backspace
128	                | KeyCode::Delete
129	                | KeyCode::Left
130	                | KeyCode::Right
131	                | KeyCode::Home
132	                | KeyCode::End
133	        )
134	    }

136	    /// Handle an action from the keymap.
137	    ///
138	    /// Returns true if the action was handled.
139	    pub fn handle_action(&mut self, action: Action) -> bool {
140	        match action {
141	            Action::MoveLeft => {
142	                self.move_left();
143	                true
144	            }
145	            Action::MoveRight => {
146	                self.move_right();
147	                true
148	            }
149	            Action::Home => {
150	                self.move_home();
151	                true
152	            }
153	            Action::End => {
154	                self.move_end();
155	                true
156	            }
157	            Action::Backspace => {
158	                self.backspace();
159	                true
160	            }
161	            Action::DeleteChar => {
162	                self.delete();
163	                true
164	            }
165	            _ => false,
166	        }
167	    }

169	    /// Handle a key event with modifiers and action mapping.
170	    ///
171	    /// This is useful when you want to handle both raw keys and mapped actions.
172	    /// Regular characters are inserted directly, while special keys go through
173	    /// action mapping if available.
174	    pub fn handle_key_with_action(
175	        &mut self,
176	        key_code: KeyCode,
177	        _modifiers: KeyModifiers,
178	        action: Option<Action>,
179	    ) -> bool {
180	        // Try action first
181	        if let Some(action) = action {
182	            if self.handle_action(action) {
183	                return true;
184	            }
185	        }
186	
187	        // Fall back to raw key handling
188	        self.handle_key(key_code)
189	    }
190	    /// Check if an action is safe to process when a text input is focused.
191	    ///
192	    /// Returns true if the action is "safe" (like navigation or text editing) and should
193	    /// be processed even when the input has focus.
194	    /// Returns false if the action should be suppressed (like 'Quit' bound to 'q') so that

216	/// Handle text input for a single character insertion
217	///
218	/// # Arguments
219	/// * `text` - Mutable reference to the text string
220	/// * `cursor_pos` - Mutable reference to cursor position
221	/// * `c` - Character to insert
222	fn handle_char_insertion(text: &mut String, cursor_pos: &mut usize, c: char) {
223	    if c.is_ascii() && !c.is_control() {
224	        let byte_index = text
225	            .char_indices()
226	            .map(|(i, _)| i)
227	            .nth(*cursor_pos)
228	            .unwrap_or(text.len());
229	        text.insert(byte_index, c);
230	        *cursor_pos = (*cursor_pos + 1).min(text.chars().count());
231	    }
232	}

234	/// Handle cursor movement
235	///
236	/// # Arguments
237	/// * `text` - The text string
238	/// * `cursor_pos` - Mutable reference to cursor position
239	/// * `key_code` - Key code (Left, Right, Home, End)
240	fn handle_cursor_movement(text: &str, cursor_pos: &mut usize, key_code: KeyCode) {
241	    match key_code {
242	        KeyCode::Left if *cursor_pos > 0 => {
243	            *cursor_pos -= 1;
244	        }
245	        KeyCode::Right => {
246	            let char_count = text.chars().count();
247	            if *cursor_pos < char_count {
248	                *cursor_pos += 1;
249	            }
250	        }
251	        KeyCode::Home => {
252	            *cursor_pos = 0;
253	        }
254	        KeyCode::End => {
255	            *cursor_pos = text.chars().count();
256	        }
257	        _ => {}
258	    }
259	}

261	/// Handle character deletion (backspace)
262	///
263	/// # Arguments
264	/// * `text` - Mutable reference to the text string
265	/// * `cursor_pos` - Mutable reference to cursor position
266	fn handle_backspace(text: &mut String, cursor_pos: &mut usize) {
267	    if *cursor_pos > 0 {
268	        let before_cursor = text.chars().take(*cursor_pos - 1);
269	        let after_cursor = text.chars().skip(*cursor_pos);
270	        *text = before_cursor.chain(after_cursor).collect();
271	        *cursor_pos -= 1;
272	    }
273	}
274	
275	/// Handle character deletion (delete key)
276	///
277	/// # Arguments
278	/// * `text` - Mutable reference to the text string
279	/// * `cursor_pos` - Mutable reference to cursor position
280	fn handle_delete(text: &mut String, cursor_pos: &mut usize) {
281	    let char_count = text.chars().count();
282	    if *cursor_pos < char_count {
283	        let before_cursor = text.chars().take(*cursor_pos);
284	        let after_cursor = text.chars().skip(*cursor_pos + 1);
285	        *text = before_cursor.chain(after_cursor).collect();
286	    }
287	}
288	/// Handle generic input for text fields (movement, editing)
289	///
290	/// # Arguments
291	/// * `text` - Mutable reference to the text string
292	/// * `cursor_pos` - Mutable reference to cursor position
293	/// * `key_code` - Key code from event
294	fn handle_input(text: &mut String, cursor_pos: &mut usize, key_code: KeyCode) {
295	    match key_code {
296	        KeyCode::Char(c) => handle_char_insertion(text, cursor_pos, c),
297	        KeyCode::Backspace => handle_backspace(text, cursor_pos),
298	        KeyCode::Delete => handle_delete(text, cursor_pos),
299	        KeyCode::Left | KeyCode::Right | KeyCode::Home | KeyCode::End => {
300	            handle_cursor_movement(text, cursor_pos, key_code);
301	        }
302	        _ => {}
303	    }
304	}

# Why Keypress Bugs Keep Recurring in Dotstate's Input Fields

## Root Cause

Dotstate's input handling relies on a **two-layer focus guard system** that is architecturally sound but frequently broken during implementation:

1. **Global layer** (`App::sync_input_mode` + `App::get_action`): Each screen's `is_input_focused()` method reports whether a text field is being edited. When true, `get_action()` suppresses navigation actions (quit, h/l/j/k under Vim keymap) and only allows essential actions (Cancel, Confirm, Backspace, arrow keys for cursor movement).

2. **Local layer** (per-screen): Every screen with text input must manually insert plain `KeyCode::Char(c)` characters **before** any keymap lookup, or Vim-bound characters like 'q'=Quit, 'h'=MoveLeft, 'j'=MoveDown will be intercepted as navigation instead of typed text.

## Why Bugs Recur

### Problem 1: Incomplete `is_input_focused()` Implementation
Several screens report focus incompletely. For example, `ManageProfilesScreen::is_input_focused()` returns `true` only when the Create popup is focused on Name or Description fields, but returns `false` when the user is in the InheritsFrom/CopyFrom list selectors. This creates a window where global keybindings fire while a user still perceives themselves as "in a form."

**Evidence**: KNOW-146 documents this divergence; the comment notes that focus is "conditionally true for Create — only when create_focused_field is Name or Description."

### Problem 2: Pattern Duplication Without Enforcement
The correct character-insertion pattern is duplicated across nearly every screen: `if let KeyCode::Char(c) = key.code { if !key.modifiers.intersects(KeyModifiers::CONTROL | KeyModifiers::ALT | KeyModifiers::SUPER) { <field>.insert_char(c); return Ok(ScreenAction::Refresh); } }`. This pattern appears in storage_setup.rs, manage_profiles.rs, profile_selection.rs, manage_packages.rs, and dotfile_selection.rs, but there is **no shared helper function or compile-time guarantee** enforcing it.

**Evidence**: KNOW-196 lists these locations and notes "Any NEW text-input screen must replicate this ordering or it will be unusable." The word "must" signals a requirement that is not machine-checked.

### Problem 3: Event Routing Doesn't Guarantee Ordering
The app's `handle_event()` flow (app.rs:650) calls `sync_input_mode()` at the start, then dispatches to the current screen's `handle_event()`. However:
- The global theme-cycling handler ('t' key) checks `input_mode_active` but is applied *before* the screen handler sees the event.
- This means a new screen that forgets to implement `is_input_focused()` will silently allow global handlers to fire (documented in KNOW-202: "the guard silently no-ops for that screen").
- A developer adding a text-input feature doesn't receive compile-time or runtime feedback if they forget either the `is_input_focused()` arm in `App::sync_input_mode()` or the per-screen character-insertion guard.

## Consequences

1. **Silent failures**: A screen missing one part of the guard (e.g., forgets `is_input_focused()` entirely) will exhibit vim-keybinding interference only under certain keymap presets (Vim/Emacs), not in the default Standard preset. This delays bug discovery.
2. **Copy-paste inconsistency**: Because the pattern is replicated, variations creep in (e.g., some screens check only `CONTROL | ALT`, others add `SUPER`, or forget to check modifiers altogether).
3. **New features at risk**: When a new screen or popup is added, developers must remember to update two locations: the `App::sync_input_mode()` match block *and* the screen's event handler. Missing either reintroduces the bug.

## Recommended Fix (Not Implemented)

Extract the character-insertion pattern into a shared `handle_char_input()` helper that returns `Some(ScreenAction::Refresh)` or `None`, used consistently in all screens. Add a compile-time assertion that every Screen implementing text inputs calls this helper in the correct place (order-enforced by refactoring into a single code path rather than duplication).

2. **Local layer** (per-screen): Every screen with text input must manually insert plain `KeyCode::Char(c)` characters **before** any keymap lookup, or Vim-bound characters like 'q'=Quit, 'h'=MoveLeft, 'j'=MoveDown will be intercepted as navigation instead of typed text.

## Why Bugs Recur

### Problem 1: Incomplete `is_input_focused()` Implementation
Several screens report focus incompletely. For example, `ManageProfilesScreen::is_input_focused()` returns `true` only when the Create popup is focused on Name or Description fields, but returns `false` when the user is in the InheritsFrom/CopyFrom list selectors. This creates a window where global keybindings fire while a user still perceives themselves as "in a form."

**Evidence**: KNOW-146 documents this divergence; the comment notes that focus is "conditionally true for Create — only when create_focused_field is Name or Description."

### Problem 2: Pattern Duplication Without Enforcement
The correct character-insertion pattern is duplicated across nearly every screen: `if let KeyCode::Char(c) = key.code { if !key.modifiers.intersects(KeyModifiers::CONTROL | KeyModifiers::ALT | KeyModifiers::SUPER) { <field>.insert_char(c); return Ok(ScreenAction::Refresh); } }`. This pattern appears in storage_setup.rs, manage_profiles.rs, profile_selection.rs, manage_packages.rs, and dotfile_selection.rs, but there is **no shared helper function or compile-time guarantee** enforcing it.

**Evidence**: KNOW-196 lists these locations and notes "Any NEW text-input screen must replicate this ordering or it will be unusable." The word "must" signals a requirement that is not machine-checked.

### Problem 3: Event Routing Doesn't Guarantee Ordering
The app's `handle_event()` flow (app.rs:650) calls `sync_input_mode()` at the start, then dispatches to the current screen's `handle_event()`. However:
- The global theme-cycling handler ('t' key) checks `input_mode_active` but is applied *before* the screen handler sees the event.
- This means a new screen that forgets to implement `is_input_focused()` will silently allow global handlers to fire (documented in KNOW-202: "the guard silently no-ops for that screen").
- A developer adding a text-input feature doesn't receive compile-time or runtime feedback if they forget either the `is_input_focused()` arm in `App::sync_input_mode()` or the per-screen character-insertion guard.

## Consequences

1. **Silent failures**: A screen missing one part of the guard (e.g., forgets `is_input_focused()` entirely) will exhibit vim-keybinding interference only under certain keymap presets (Vim/Emacs), not in the default Standard preset. This delays bug discovery.
2. **Copy-paste inconsistency**: Because the pattern is replicated, variations creep in (e.g., some screens check only `CONTROL | ALT`, others add `SUPER`, or forget to check modifiers altogether).
3. **New features at risk**: When a new screen or popup is added, developers must remember to update two locations: the `App::sync_input_mode()` match block *and* the screen's event handler. Missing either reintroduces the bug.

## Recommended Fix (Not Implemented)

Extract the character-insertion pattern into a shared `handle_char_input()` helper that returns `Some(ScreenAction::Refresh)` or `None`, used consistently in all screens. Add a compile-time assertion that every Screen implementing text inputs calls this helper in the correct place (order-enforced by refactoring into a single code path rather than duplication).
